name: Garo (A'chik)

ancestors.notes: Garo is a Boro-Garo (Bodo-Garo) language, Brahmaputran/Sal branch, Sino-Tibetan.

notes: Garo (A'chik), spoken mainly in Meghalaya, India (and Bangladesh). Boro-Garo branch, Sino-Tibetan. Latin script is the PRIMARY modern orthography (20 letters plus an apostrophe 'raka' for the glottal stop /ʔ/), developed from 1902 by American Baptist missionaries and replacing an earlier Bengali-script orthography used from the 1840s-1924 (Wikipedia; Burling 2004). Bengali script is noted here as the historical/administrative alternative but not modelled, per the task brief (Latin primary). Voiceless stops are aspirated word-initially, spelled with postposed ⟨h⟩ digraphs (⟨ph th kh ch⟩), a single-phoneme reading (AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨ng⟩ spells the velar nasal /ŋ/. The vowel letter ⟨i⟩ represents both /i/ and /ɨ/ depending on syllable position (Burling 2004) -- encoded as allophone candidates on the same grapheme rather than as two competing keys, since the choice is positional/predictable, not a separate spelling. Garo has no phonemic tone; instead it contrasts syllables closed by glottal stop vs. open syllables (Burling 2004; Wikipedia), which is why the glottal-stop grapheme ⟨'⟩ is retained as a real, distinctive letter rather than dropped as 'just punctuation'. ⟨c ch⟩ spell the alveolo-palatal affricates /tɕ tɕʰ/ per Wikipedia's Garo consonant chart (corrected from an earlier postalveolar reading); the same source states voiceless stops /p t k/ are always aspirated word-initially [pʰ tʰ kʰ].
